title: Hubble image of the Meathook Galaxy
caption: The Meathook Galaxy, NGC 2442, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 2442, SN 1999ga · constellation Volans · about 55 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: In this close-up, Hubble zooms in on the Meathook Galaxy, NGC 2442, focusing on its central regions and the more compact of its two lopsided spiral arms. The galaxy lies about 55 million light-years away in the southern constellation Volans.

That arm has a history. In 1999, a supernova exploded there, the bright death of a star. Hubble made these observations in 2006 specifically to study what the explosion left behind. A supernova can briefly outshine an entire galaxy, and looking back at the site years later helps astronomers learn about the star that exploded and its surroundings.

To complete the frame, parts of the image's edges were filled in with ground-based data from the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, so the picture blends observations from space and from Chile's La Silla site.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.38 x 3.29 arcminutes) and distance (55 million light years), the frame spans roughly 38,000 × 53,000 light-years. Its light set out about 55 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Planetary Camera 2, with blue, near-infrared and H-alpha filters, plus ground-based data at the edges. The packet does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The near-infrared part of the data is invisible to the eye, and this level of detail is far beyond what an eye could see.
